refnamediv.refpurpose: pass a name through the DNS name qualification rules

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: dnsqual feeds dn through name qualification. It prints the resultant name, or (if search paths are configured) list of names, 1 per line. See djbdns-client5 for how name qualification operates.
Normally dnsqual exits 0. If it encounters a temporary problem that prevents it from performing name qualification, it prints an error message and exits 111.
refsection.note: dnsqual outputs names as they would then be passed to DNS lookup in assumed-fully-qualified form (e.g. as the fqdn input to dnsq1). This does not use a trailing dot as a marker. It is an error to pass the output names to something that will do name qualification again.

Name qualification by itself does no renormalization of names that contain non-alphanumeric characters or octal escape sequences. That is done when a fqdn is converted to and from the on-the-wire DNS protocol form by DNS lookup.

refsection.title: History
refsection.para: dnsqual was an addition to Daniel J. Bernstein's djbdns toolset by Jonathan de Boyne Pollard.

refsection.para: Original code and documentation by Jonathan de Boyne Pollard.
